newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam says China has proposed talks next week.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam says China has proposed talks next week.

text.p: China has proposed to Vietnam that the two sides hold expert-level talks on a disputed area in the South China Sea next week, Vietnam's foreign minister Nguyen Manh Cam said on Wednesday.

"We have asked for discussions between experts as soon as possible. China has proposed next week. The location is going to be discussed. We have asked for it to be in Hanoi but Beijing has been proposed, and perhaps we are going to accept it."

Cam, speaking to reporters after the opening of the National Assembly spring session, said talks were necessary because China was drilling for oil in an area which Vietnam considers as its own territory.
Communist party secretary-general Do Muoi told reporters that China had accepted Hanoi's proposal for talks.
He said that Vietnam had raised its voice more than usual this time because quiet diplomacy had not been effective.

Beijing said on Tuesday it was preparing for negotiations with Vietnam. Hanoi last week restated its claim to the area of the South China Sea, some 64.5 nautical miles off its central coast and 71.5 nautical miles from China's Hainan island.
